## What I built

A new **`python3 -m remote_control manager`** subcommand — the autonomous session shepherd you described — following the repo's conventions (pure decision core + thin I/O, dry-run default, unit-tested):

- **`remote_control/manager.py`** — classification + decision core + dry-run planner
- **`remote_control/config.py`** — added `ManagerConfig` (grace/cooldown/allowlist/dry-run env knobs)
- **`remote_control/cli.py`** — wired the `manager` subcommand
- **`tests/test_manager.py`** — 42 tests; **full suite 300 green**

It reuses the existing detectors (`usage_limit.detect`, `inventory`, `session_list`) rather than re-deriving state. The **decision table** runs in priority order, scoped to repos in `active-dirs.txt` (host-aware):

| Signal | → Action |
|---|---|
| `requires_action` past answer-grace | **answer** — `claude -p` investigator drafts the reply, POST it back |
| idle past done-grace, connected | **review** — investigator returns `DONE:`→recommend `/close-work`, else `NEXT:` |
| `disconnected` past rescue-grace | **rescue** — fork → resume fork → archive original |
| usage-limit paused | **defer** (usage-monitor owns it) |
| running / too-recent | **skip** |

**Live dry-run against your real sessions worked** — it classified all 6, held the two genuinely-waiting FamilyFund sessions behind the answer-grace (`question only 10s old`), and skipped this session as `running`. Guardrails: dry-run default ON, grace + cooldown + max-actions-per-tick, its own `agent-manager.log`/`-state.json`.

## One correction worth flagging

I initially wrote the files into the **main checkout** (`~/dev/ai-harness/`) instead of this worktree — the explore agents reported main-checkout absolute paths and I followed them. I relocated all four files into the worktree and **restored the main checkout to clean** (verified: `git status` empty there; the only dirty files were the four I'd created this session). Everything above is now in the worktree on its branch, uncommitted.

## The gate to going live (`--go`)

`--go` intentionally isn't wired yet — answering/archiving live sessions is hard to undo. Two things need verifying against the real API first: (1) reading a **cloud** session's pending-question text (local-transcript read already covers bridge sessions), and (2) the **archive** verb (`PUT /sessions/{id}` `{status:archived}`).
